teacherNotes.title: Core Words
teacherNotes.content: age, old, year, birthday, month, January, February, March, April, May, June, July, August, September, October, November, December, party, cake

elements.content: Core Active Vocabulary (10-20 items):
age, old, year, birthday, month, January, February, March, April, May, June, July, August, September, October, November, December, party, cake
Essential Chunks & Functional Collocations:

• How old are you? (asking age)
• I am 20 years old (stating age)
• When is your birthday? (asking birthday month)
• My birthday is in May (stating birthday month)
• Happy Birthday! (congratulating)

teacherNotes.title: Phonetic Aim
teacherNotes.content: Month stress patterns: 'January, 'February, Sep'tember, Oc'tober. Linking 'How old are you?' /haʊ əʊld ɑː juː/.

elements.content: Pronunciation Focus:
Month stress patterns: 'January, 'February, Sep'tember, Oc'tober. Linking 'How old are you?' /haʊ əʊld ɑː juː/.

teacherNotes.title: Function-First Grammar Rule
teacherNotes.content: Using verb 'be' for age ('I am 20', NOT 'I have 20'). Possessive determiners 'my', 'your', 'his', 'her' with birthday.

elements.content: Grammar System & Functional Framing:
Using verb 'be' for age ('I am 20', NOT 'I have 20'). Possessive determiners 'my', 'your', 'his', 'her' with birthday.
Examples:

• How old are you?
• I am 19 years old.
• How old is he?
• He is 20.
• When is her birthday?
• Her birthday is in July.
Reading Dialogue & Script:

Script using target language:
Person A: How old are you?
Person B: I am 20 years old
Listening Comprehension Prompt: Listen to the prompt and confirm understanding.
